Relic

REL-ik -- shares a root with 'relinquish,' meaning to leave behind. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Relic is an object or item from the past that has survived to the present day.

The museum's oldest relic was a bronze coin dated to the fourth century.

Worked Example

A farmer plowing his field strikes something hard with his tractor blade and unearths a rusted sword that has been buried underground since a battle fought eight hundred years ago.

That surviving object from a much earlier time is exactly what a relic is. Unlike 'replica,' which is a modern copy, a relic is the genuine, original surviving item.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

artifact: an object made or used by people in the past, of historical interest

heirloom: a valuable object passed down through generations of a family

remnant: a small remaining part of something larger

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

replica: an exact copy of something, especially on a smaller scale

reproduction: a copy of an original work or object

Where it sits · how much history the leftover carries — remnant → relic → artifact

remnant vs. relic: Remnant is broader than relic -- a remnant can be any small leftover piece of something, while relic specifically emphasizes a surviving object valued for its historical age and significance.

artifact vs. relic: Artifact can feel more precise than relic in some contexts: relic often suggests something treasured or almost sacred from the past, while artifact is the more neutral, scientific term archaeologists use for any human-made object.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back (Latin)

Root — lic

Root — lic: to leave (from Latin linquere, 'to leave'; relinquere, 'to leave behind' — the same piece is spelled linqu in relinquish)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- ('back') + lic ('to leave' — from Latin linquere; relinquere meant 'to leave behind,' and the same piece is spelled linqu in relinquish): a relic, at its root, is something left behind — a surviving remnant of an earlier time.

Use the root in a new word: relinquish

Use the root in a new word: relinquish: After years of ownership, the family finally decided to relinquish the old farmhouse to the historical society.

Word Choice

Relic often describes a physical object, but can also be used figuratively for an outdated custom or idea, as in 'a relic of a bygone era.'
